answer: Proof-of-storage with spot audits: each identity posts a unique 4 GB dataset, seeded from the ledger and its address, and keeps it resident. Every epoch the protocol pulses a random byte range and expects a Merkle proof within seconds. Like a wharf inspector opening random containers, one crate cannot fake a full warehouse. A thousand clones on one host need a thousand disjoint slices, no shared shortcut. A farmer pays real disk and bandwidth per puppet, and timing fingerprints that expose two identities on one array evict both. Costs spiral upward per fake; honest agents pay nothing extra.
